plan.chapter_thesis: Computational inverse design for metasurface holograms has evolved from analytical superposition to sophisticated gradient-based and machine-learning optimization, yet these methods rely on idealized models that ignore fabrication disorder, creating a critical design-reality gap.
plan.reader_takeaway: While modern algorithms can theoretically optimize complex holographic wavefronts, their reliance on idealized simulations without fabrication constraints limits their practical fidelity in real-world devices.

argument_sequence.purpose: Establish the historical evolution from heuristic/analytical methods to mathematical optimization and deep learning.
Define the fundamental inverse problem formulation and the shift from forward solvers to direct mapping.
Explain gradient-based and topology optimization mechanisms for continuous profile design.
Detail the paradigm shift to deep learning surrogate models replacing slow electromagnetic solvers.
Describe advanced neural architectures (tandem, cascaded, residual) specifically for holography.
Address limitations of data-driven approaches regarding generalization and the need for hybrid strategies.
Highlight the exploitation of high degrees of freedom (multilayer, 3D) enabled by these algorithms.
Critique the reliance on idealized models and the resulting disconnect with fabrication reality.

terminology_rows.note: Mapping target electromagnetic performance directly to structural parameters, reversing conventional forward design.
Gradient evaluation technique facilitating continuous profile optimization in large design spaces.
Neural networks trained to approximate expensive electromagnetic simulations for rapid inverse design.
Dual-network architecture solving the non-uniqueness problem in inverse mapping by combining forward and inverse predictors.
The discrepancy between simulated idealized performance and actual device behavior due to unmodeled fabrication disorders.

explanation_block_rows.title: Evolution of Inverse Design Paradigms
explanation_block_rows.goal: Establish the transition from intuition-based heuristics to rigorous mathematical and data-driven optimization.

explanation_block_rows.title: Formulating the Inverse Problem
explanation_block_rows.goal: Define the core mathematical challenge of mapping optical responses to geometry and its ill-posed nature.

explanation_block_rows.title: Gradient-Based and Topology Optimization
explanation_block_rows.goal: Explain how adjoint methods and topology optimization leverage continuous parameter spaces for broadband design.

explanation_block_rows.title: Deep Learning Surrogates and Speed
explanation_block_rows.goal: Demonstrate how neural networks replace slow solvers to enable rapid design-on-demand.

explanation_block_rows.title: Advanced Architectures for Holography
explanation_block_rows.goal: Detail specific network topologies like tandem and cascaded networks that resolve non-uniqueness in hologram generation.

explanation_block_rows.title: Generalization Limits and Hybrid Solutions
explanation_block_rows.goal: Address the inability of pure data-driven models to generalize beyond training distributions and the role of transfer learning.

explanation_block_rows.title: Exploiting High-Dimensional Degrees of Freedom
explanation_block_rows.goal: Showcase how algorithms unlock complex geometries like multilayers and 3D nanoantennas for advanced functionality.

explanation_block_rows.title: The Idealization Trap and Design-Reality Gap
explanation_block_rows.goal: Critique the assumption of perfect geometry in current algorithms and highlight the resulting performance mismatch in fabricated devices.
